### Worship in the Dark
Author: Jonathan Parnell
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/worship-in-the-dark
Passage: Psalm 88:18
Points:
- Psalm 88 is unusual because it offers no immediate earthly resolution and concludes in darkness.
- Even when submerged under overwhelming sorrow, the psalmist keeps speaking directly to God.
- Believers do not need to hide their anguish, because God is never intimidated by our darkest moments.
- Jesus endured total abandonment and the grave so that his people never walk through grief alone.
- Through Christ's resurrection, believers are given grace and strength to worship even in the shadows.

### How I Gleaned Hope from the Darkest Psalm
Author: Christina Fox
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/how-i-gleaned-hope-from-the-darkest-psalm/
Passage: Psalm 88:1-18
Points:
- Believers have full permission to direct their uninhibited sorrow and cries for help toward God.
- The psalms teach that worship includes raw honesty rather than superficial pretending.
- Scripture refuses to peddle quick fixes, recognizing the lingering pain of living in a fallen world.
- The psalmist's unresolved cry points forward to Christ, who bore our griefs and intercedes on our behalf.

### Yes, God Does Care: Praying Through Despair With Psalm 88
Author: Craig Groeschel
Site: Bible Gateway News & Knowledge
URL: https://www.biblegateway.com/learn/biblical-living/comfort/praying-depair-psalm-88/
Passage: Psalm 88:3-18
Points:
- God cares deeply about mental and emotional anguish, validating our distress by including this psalm in Scripture.
- Heman was a respected leader and worshiper who nevertheless endured severe, enduring depression.
- God does not require tidy, cheerful prayers, but invites sincere honesty about our pain.
- Because Jesus lived a human life, he personally understands our deepest emotional struggles.
- Suffering believers can confidently approach God's throne of grace to receive mercy and help.
